s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal pain with radiation to the back, associated with anorexia and malaise, and a cystic mass in the pancreas
salient_findings: Vague, colicky epigastric pain radiating to the interscapular region
Cystic lesion in the head of the pancreas on abdominal ultrasound
Elevated platelet count and blood urea
key_facts: One-year history of epigastric pain
Pain relieved by changes in sitting position
Pain worsened by eating
No history of alcohol use, abdominal trauma, or pancreatitis
Thrombocytosis with platelet count >1 000 000/µL
Elevated blood urea
Cystic mass in the pancreatic head on CT scan
Serum CA 19-9 level within normal range
Mild epigastric tenderness on deep palpation
No signs of portal hypertension

shortlist.label: Intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass in the pancreatic head and epigastric pain

shortlist.label: Mucinous cystic neoplasm
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass in the pancreatic head and elevated blood urea

shortlist.label: Serous cystadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass in the pancreatic head and absence of invasion or lymphadenopathy

shortlist.label: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass in the pancreatic head and thrombocytosis

shortlist.label: Pancreatic pseudocyst
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass in the pancreatic head and history of epigastric pain

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a large, well-circumscribed cystic mass in the pancreatic head, without invasion of adjacent organs or lymphadenopathy, and a normal serum CA 19-9 level, is more consistent with a mucinous cystic neoplasm, which is a type of pancreatic cystic neoplasm that can cause epigastric pain and has a variable prognosis.

rejected.label: Intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm
rejected.why: IPMNs are typically smaller and have a more complex appearance on imaging, and often have an elevated serum CA 19-9 level.

rejected.label: Serous cystadenoma
rejected.why: Serous cystadenomas are usually smaller, have a more characteristic 'sponge-like' appearance on imaging, and are less likely to cause significant symptoms.

rejected.label: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The lack of invasion of adjacent organs or lymphadenopathy, and a normal serum CA 19-9 level, makes pancreatic adenocarcinoma less likely.

rejected.label: Pancreatic pseudocyst
rejected.why: The patient's lack of history of pancreatitis or abdominal trauma, and the well-circumscribed nature of the cystic mass, makes a pancreatic pseudocyst less likely.
